page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.8xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine delivered via the AWS Nitro System. The server is configured with a dedicated Intel Xeon 8252C processor providing 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at sustained clock rates up to 4.5 GHz, supported by 24 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 vector execution extensions. Memory capacity is provisioned at 1024 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, establishing a dense ratio of 32 GB per vCPU. Network throughput is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps. The instance provides no hardware accelerators, with a GPU count of zero, and includes no local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent data access requires Elastic Block Store (EBS) attachments.

Empirical benchmarks indicate performance characteristics skewed heavily toward memory operations and high-frequency execution. In synthetic memory testing, the instance achieved a top-quartile write bandwidth of 97.33 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB blocks and a PassMark memory score of 2872.25. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 31.71 GB/sec, also in the top tier. General compute benchmarks reflect median performance, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 12,403.0 and stress-ng multi-core recording 39,010.24. CPU-based machine learning inference is a notable constraint; while prompt processing on smaller models remains within average bounds, generation throughput drops sharply on larger architectures, recording 8.26 tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

The physical resource balance makes the x2iezn.8xlarge a specialized architectural selection. Organizations pay for extreme memory allocation and high interconnect throughput rather than massive core counts or local flash storage. It offers high cost efficiency for memory-constrained workloads where RAM capacity dictates the cluster footprint, eliminating the need to overprovision CPU cores simply to satisfy memory demands. Recommended workloads include large in-memory key-value databases such as Redis, enterprise in-memory relational platforms, electronic design automation (EDA), and real-time big data caching engines.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, designed for workloads requiring extreme RAM capacity. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8252C processor capable of 4.5 GHz, paired with 1024 GB of DDR4-3000 memory. This configuration provides a high 32:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, accompanied by a 75 Gbps network interface. The instance contains no bundled GPUs and no local disk storage, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-quartile uncached memory write throughput of 97.33 GB/sec and strong compression performance, balanced against average general-purpose compute scores. By maximizing memory density without requiring proportional core scale-out, x2iezn.8xlarge provides an efficient hardware allocation for in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, and large-scale data caching layers.
